verdicts.reason: Read the abstract and full text: Born reciprocity (x,p)->(p,-x) maps charges in a magnetic charge density onto closed strings in R-flux, a 3-form flux over momentum space, i.e. a background. The full text has no 'monopole(s) in momentum space' and no 'dark matter' (grep: 0), and says reciprocity 'is not a natural symmetry of the magnetic Poisson brackets'. Not overstated, and not understated: it places no objects in momentum space.

new_findings.citation: S. Majid, B. J. Schroers, "q-Deformation and Semidualisation in 3d Quantum Gravity", J. Phys. A 42, 425402 (2009), arXiv:0806.2587
new_findings.summary: In euclidean 3d quantum gravity, 'quantum Born reciprocity' or semidualisation, a quantum-group operation that interchanges position and momentum, relates the effective noncommutative models. Under it a particle's irreducible representations are realized as 'monopole sections' on spheres in position space on one side and, after a noncommutative Fourier transform, on fuzzy spheres in noncommutative momentum space on the other.
new_findings.difference: The 'monopole sections' are the carrier spaces of irreducible representations labelled by mass and spin, functions that 'arise as sections of Dirac monopole bundles' (monopole harmonics), not magnetically charged matter. Nothing is placed in momentum space as objects; no abundance, dark matter or detection. It is the collision a reader meets when searching Born reciprocity with monopoles in momentum space.

quotes.text: The latter is an algebraic operation defined using quantum group methods that interchanges position and momentum.
a noncommutative Fourier transform gives us a picture of the irreps for this model as noncommutative monopole sections on fuzzy spheres in noncommutative momentum space
The two ‘physical models’ here are equivalent under Fourier transform and an exchange of position and momentum.

new_findings.citation: Y. Pan, R. Yin, "Constructing Berry-Maxwell equations with Lorentz invariance and Gauss's law of Weyl monopoles in four-dimensional energy-momentum space", Phys. Rev. B 110, 075139 (2024), arXiv:2308.00612
new_findings.summary: Builds a 'reciprocal electromagnetic field' in 4D energy-momentum space by extending Berry curvature, with Weyl points acting as magnetic-like monopoles whose density and current source 'Berry-Maxwell equations'. The body text, read by the verifier in the arXiv PDF (lit.py and WebFetch could not reach it), invokes Born reciprocity between the Berry four-connection and the electromagnetic four-potential to construct those equations, and attributes their duality and self-duality with Maxwell's equations to Born reciprocity. INSPIRE's full-text index also matches 'Born reciprocity' and 'magnetic monopole' in it. This was the searcher's unread lead: an explicit Born-reciprocity construction of an electromagnetism in momentum space whose magnetic charges are momentum-space monopoles.
new_findings.difference: The monopoles are Berry-curvature (Weyl) monopoles of electronic bands, the 'right geometry, different flux' of #11 §11.1, not magnetically charged solitons of a matter sector. No matter localized in momentum, no abundance, no dark matter (0 matches) and no null-result argument. Of the shared mechanism (Born reciprocity placing magnetic sources in momentum space) it is the nearest in wording found; of the object, a collision.

quotes.text: We present the construction of a reciprocal electromagnetic field by extending the Berry curvatures into four-dimensional (4D) energy-momentum space.
we find that the physical reality of this reciprocal electromagnetic field is rooted in the fundamental principles of special relativity and Gauss's law of Weyl monopoles

not_found_assessment.reason: Holds. My own searches covered Born's reciprocity papers forward, curved momentum space and relative locality, the Yang and Snyder models, two-time physics, Majid's quantum Born reciprocity, the dual cosmologies, phase-space, dual-space, velocity-space and k-space phrasings, physics.gen-ph, Crossref and the web. Nothing places magnetically charged objects in momentum space as matter, abundant or dark. What exists is backgrounds (the R-flux as the momentum-space image of a smeared magnetic charge; Berard-Mohrbach's dual monopole field of the vacuum) and Berry-curvature or representation-theoretic 'monopoles' in momentum space, now including two in an explicit Born-reciprocity setting: Pan-Yin 2024 (Weyl monopoles as sources of a reciprocal electromagnetism) and Majid-Schroers 2009 (monopole sections in noncommutative momentum space). Monopole dark matter as such is prior art in many position-space forms, which the statement does not deny.

Holds in substance, with one qualifier on wording. Condensed matter has 'momentum-space skyrmions', topological textures of band spinors over the Brillouin zone (Onoda-Tatara-Nagaosa 2004; Mohanta-Kampf-Kopp 2017), and even speaks of 'the duality between real and momentum spaces' for skyrmion number. These are textures of a field defined on momentum space, not solitons of a matter field localized in momentum by their own topology, so the statement stands; a reader will meet the words. I found no paper localizing a soliton in momentum by topology, and none computing monopoles whose field profile is spread wider than the galactic coherence length (Parker-bound search: 16 hits, none).

Holds. Searches on conjugate space and universe, dual cosmologies, Born's own circle, gen-ph, Crossref and the web found other hiding places (a second time dimension, 'another space-time', hidden sectors, monopolium, magnetic screening, noncommutative spacetime, sub-Dirac charges, superluminal kinematics, unobservability) and cosmological histories, but none in momentum space and none using Born reciprocity. Two qualifiers. (1) Govaerts 2023 does link the mutual electromagnetic darkness of magnetic and electric matter to the need to reassess monopole searches; it is the nearest physical analogue, by force law, not localization. (2) One item is unread: S. Khademi, 'Why magnetic monopoles are not seen?' (2009 conference paper, Maltepe University open-access repository, HTTP 403). A search engine's summary says it invokes uncertainty in phase-space quantum mechanics, the one lead that might bear on C3's mechanism; it should be obtained before the statement is called final.

notes: Verdict: the searcher's findings stand. All 53 identifiers resolve with title, authors, year and venue matching; all 72 quotes re-run FOUND (two loose matches are exact in the source's rendering: 'R -flux', '1017 GeV/c2'). No relation is overstated into anticipation (none was claimed) and none is understated: no paper states C2 or C3. Corrections: (a) Govaerts 2023 (C3): the difference text says the paper does not present the darkness as an explanation of the null result. True, but its conclusion does say the formulation 'requires an earnest reassessment of ... experiments that have been pursued over the decades in search of the existence of magnetic monopoles'; worth stating. (b) Kobayashi-Perri 2023: evidence-against only below ~1e18 GeV; its conclusions also allow Dirac-charged monopoles that cluster with the Galaxy as all of the dark matter as far as Parker bounds go. Zhang et al. 2024 disfavour 1e16-1e20 GeV using the Andromeda Parker bound. The published evidence against position-localized monopoles of our photon as the dark matter is therefore agreed below ~1e18 GeV and contested between these two papers from ~1e18 to ~1e20 GeV. All four evidence-against items assume objects localized in position; none tests p-localization. (c) Brummer et al. 2025: evidence-against a minimal separate-photon realization with ordinary thermal history, which is #14's model, already dead with Paul's concurrence; it does not reach the conjecture as stated. (d) Kimura-Sasaki-Shiozawa 2022 and Gregory-Harvey-Moore 1997 are weak links (the first only recalls others' results); confidence low. (e) Ellis 2022: the citation's '(non-mainstream)' grades the work beyond the brief's venue statement. New findings: three, all C2 and none prior art. Majid-Schroers 2009 (collision: 'monopole sections' in noncommutative momentum space under quantum Born reciprocity).
